Stycast 1090SI functions as an effective alternative to polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) for constructing test samples when the material's homogeneous internal structure prevents light scattering. However, because Stycast 1090SI is transparent, its use necessitates embedding scatterers if the objective is to study light scattering phenomena. The reported study outlines the methodology for determining the acoustic properties of both pure Stycast 1090SI and various acoustic-optical block fillings using through-transmission techniques. The findings indicate that the material behaves as a non-dispersive medium across the frequency ranges examined and shows strong acoustic similarity to PMMA, differing by less than 3%. The sole notable exception occurs in bulk attenuation for these fillings composites, where attenuation is found to be approximately 1 dB/cm lower than that of PMMA.

Multilayer networks serve as essential tools for modeling and analyzing intricate systems characterized by layered interactions. While recent research has highlighted various methods for assessing node significance within these structures, this study focuses on how interlayer constraints influence and propagate importance metrics across different layers. By examining standard interlayer dependency models, we demonstrate that the significance of a node in any given layer is determined not only by its intrinsic local and global attributes within that specific layer but also critically by the importance nodes in other connected layers. Although existing calculation methods employ varying interlayer mapping techniques, they fundamentally rely on the significance of nodes across linked layers to establish a node's overall standing. Furthermore, we introduce and evaluate several novel interlayer mapping approaches using well-known importance metrics across diverse multilayer examples, finding that our proposed methods generally yield more robust and stable results. Finally, we analyze standard power iteration algorithms and associated matrix constructions employed in these calculations, identifying shortcomings that can lead to erroneous significance assessments; consequently, we suggest specific modifications and present revised iteration algorithms that address these deficiencies.

Most cameras exhibit a point-spread function (PSF) that shifts with the color of light, causing color images to suffer from blurring at some wavelengths while experiencing high contrast elsewhere. In this article, an approach utilizing the deterministic optimization of a diffraction-motivated design is proposed to create a uniform PSF across all wavelengths. Achieving uniformity demands bending the PSF edges inward to counteract natural diffraction-induced broadening on the image corners. Our design methodology involves optimizing the pupil function to equalize PSF dimensions in both size and form factor throughout the field of view for every color. A sample system developed through this method produced a consistent PSF across the entire image for three distinct wavelengths, with the calculated 10‑to‑90 percent rise/flat times differing by less than 20 percent between corners and the optical axis.

While Android has become a dominant mobile platform, its openness allows malicious actors to distribute harmful apps easily. To mitigate these security risks, Google introduced Play Protect, an anti-malware solution integrated into the Google Play Store that scans apps before and after installation. Unfortunately, the certification required for the store does not guarantee security, allowing malicious code to remain in the marketplace. OctopOS is a timely light-weight virtual operating system image designed to address the limitations of Play Protect. It replaces the standard Android runtime with a secure sandbox, ensuring that only verified safe applications run on the device. By scanning every system call and verifying the integrity of the executing binary against a cached image, OctopOS detects and halts malicious behavior before an installation is finalized. Evaluations indicate that this system blocks all known malware from the initial release of Play Shield without triggering false positives, operating at a minimal cost in terms of performance.

Deviating from prior work that limits attacks to slight perturbations within nearly flawless trajectories, our framework acknowledges that limited but catastrophic disruptions can still arise. We first establish that standard policy learning, even the most robust variants, are vulnerable to these few bad episodes and can be fundamentally derailed. For isolated brown dwarfs and planets, the one-dimensional stellar structure equations determine the shape of a non-rotating object's critical curve, which delineates the initial-structure-age tracks in the theoretical evolution diagram. Under the assumption that $J_{\rm limit}$ aligns with values derived from the double-stripe instability, a substellar object beginning with an age of $10$ gyr on the hydrogen-burning trail will deplete its fuel supply roughly $2.5-4\times$ faster than a non-rotating counterpart if its initial rotation surpasses the threshold ($J > J_{\rm limit}$). Consequently, the inclusion of these rapid-rotation tracks allows the hydrogen-burning trail to extend beyond the maximum ages currently observed in the substellar population. Additionally, our results suggest that planets and brown dwarves initiating with rotation rates exceeding the threshold will migrate toward lower-gravity regions of the theoretical evolution diagram as they age, potentially resolving the discrepancy regarding the presence of low-gravity brown dwarves older than $10$ gyr.

Third-generation wireless communication systems and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) are becoming increasingly vital, given their extensive applications in sensor and Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Within this model, general antenna selection ensures that base station antennas are continuously dedicated to either harvesting energy or decoding incoming signals for specific users. From an implementation standpoint, this system operates solely through a hardware configuration, requiring no updates to current information or power transmission protocols from users or other network elements. Unlike previous approaches using fixed harvesting/decoding arrangements, the proposed method functions dynamically throughout the harvesting and service cycles, thereby maximizing the efficiency of energy harvesting. Using this general scheme, we derive the cumulative distribution function (CDF) and probability density function (PDF) for harvested power, along with outages for decoding. Object Detection has become an indispensable part of our daily lives, supporting a wide range of applications. Many people rely on it to handle tasks involving objects of different sizes. Most current models use the Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) architecture. This design merges high-resolution, low-level features with coarse, semantic features to identify objects across various scales. However, this current approach often results in the original high-level semantic features being downsampled and losing detail, which can hurt performance. To solve this, we created a new framework called Hierarchical Multi-level Feature Pyramid Networks (HM-FPN). This design keeps the original strong high-level features intact and combines them with detailed low-level features to form features that are rich in detail and strong in meaning. This combination significantly improves detection results for both small and large objects compared to standard FPN backbones. We tested our model using two famous networks, ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B4. Our results show major improvements over the original FPN versions, especially when detecting small objects. We also checked our work on the COCO dataset. Our final results show that our model beats many other top-tier detectors, like RetinaNet-HM-FPN, which improved by 2.3% mAP, and EfficientNets with FPN, which saw gains of 2.2% mAP.

Conditional quantile regression offers a robust framework for analyzing the dependence between variables, particularly for capturing non-Equity relationships and varying tail behaviors in robust ways. As demonstrated by simulated examples and empirical data, the proposed method yields reliable asymptotic estimates for variable extreme quantiles and mediocres.

We conclude by outlining the dependencies of this mechanism regarding physical parameters and temporal evolution, suggesting that global magnetic clustering represents a viable route for creating planetesimal building blocks.

Using a correlated Hartree-Fock method, we analyze SrMnO$_3$ within an $e_g$-filled $t$-$J$ model. Although the hole density around oxygen atoms and the local moment character of the electronic ground state remain largely unchanged, the predicted spectral profiles differ markedly. Specifically, the related energy bands are rotated in momentum space relative to one another, producing a distinct dual-peaked structure in the spectrum that is absent when these orbitals are uncorrelated. These dual bands are attributed to Mn $3d$ and O $2$p character, respectively, with the second band arising solely through cross-term hopping induced by the two correlated orbitals. Consequently, this dual-peaked dual-gap structure serves as a signature for the model including the remote correlated orbitals, potentially explaining features in SrIrO$_3$ observed in SrMnO$_3$-related systems.

Accumulating high-quality multi-qubit entanglement serves as a fundamental requirement for numerous protocols in scalable quantum computing and communication. This study examines the engineering of Mølmer-Sørensen (MS) gate sequences designed for three-qubit chains of trapped ions, with a focus on their frequency robustness and efficiency. We demonstrate that an effective strategy involves constructing entanglement-rich states directly into the target diagonal (spin-boson basis) states of the system. By employing a single biquadratic MS gate tailored for specific frequency mismatched conditions, the proposed framework forces the creation of exact diagonal components in both the target and adjacent off-target diagonals. This mechanism enables the generation of multiple qubit entanglements simply by operating different trapping frequencies, a solution that significantly enhances method resilience against dephasing caused by atomic mode instability. Furthermore, we detail a stepwise execution approach for these optimized protocols over extended periods, which matches the system's natural timescales, thereby minimizing single-point failures and reducing faults caused by stochastic fluctuations in pulse timing. Numerical simulations confirm that under typical experimental parameters, the resulting three-party Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state fidelity surpasses 0.98. Comparative results indicate that this strategy outperforms existing approaches regarding frequency robustness and overall performance.

By summing these components, we present a comprehensive equation of state for B cation stress. This enhanced volume-dependent formulation correctly predicts A cation-driven B cation symmetry breaking trends, including the stabilization of specific crystal systems such as amantane, rhombic, and monoclinc phases. Notably, our findings reveal a linear correlation between B cation stress and equilibrium volume, alongside linear and nonlinear relationships dependent on filler A cations. Importantly, this linear trend holds true regardless of whether the resulting symmetry breaking is consistent within a single perovskite family or varies among multiple families. The accurate prediction capabilities of our model extend effectively to both occupied and unexplored regions of the A cation and volume parameter space. Uniquely, our equation of state offers a practical tool for anticipating the correct symmetry breaking in perovskites even when experimental data is lacking.

Select K-fold cross-validation is a widely adopted technique for performance assessment machine-learning models and data mining. In this approach, the dataset is randomly segmented into $K$ partitions of roughly equal size. Each subset functions as a test set exactly once, while the remaining subsets serve as training data. However, because data distribution across these folds is guaranteed only in expectation, data skew can occur within individual folds and between pairs, potentially causing cross-validation performance metrics to fluctuate. To address this issue, we introduce J-K-fold cross-validation, which stochastically generates multiple standard K-fold configurations and aggregates their results to yield a final performance estimate. We demonstrate through both synthetic data experiments and analysis of crossing-validation outcomes on on real-world datasets that this proposed method yields significantly more stable measurements compared to traditional K-fold cross-validation, thereby enhancing results without incurring additional computational costs.

Semantic segmentation is a critical computer vision task with widespread applications, typically relying on large network architectures that often struggle with limited onboard resources in edge devices. While knowledge distillation techniques using Teacher-Student frameworks have effectively enabled lightweight student networks to match the performance of massive teacher models, they do not inherently guarantee that the student outperforms the teacher in terms of efficiency and speed. This paper introduces a novel Super Teacher-Student (SuperTS) architecture designed to mutually enhance both the Super Student and the Teacher. Specifically, high-confidence soft labels from the Super Teacher guide multiple lightweight student branches, which in turn provide knowledge feedback to improve the Super Teacher's performance through a dynamic self-adaptive mechanism. Our method breaks the conventional assumption that teacher models must always exceed students in size, introducing instead the concept of a "super" model that can surpass the teacher in capability. Experiments across three distinct datasets demonstrate that this approach significantly boosts overall model efficiency, allowing heavily pruned student variants to outperform not only the original teacher but also advanced distillation methods, including the reportable PASCOCV 2021. As one tangible outcome on the CityPersons dataset, the resulting SuperTS system achieves a real-time 35.8 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano while delivering 94.85 mJOS for judgment, representing a 30.80 mJOS improvement over prior state-of-the-art models.

Bucket Elimination serves as a versatile algorithm for both optimization and inference within graphical models. Using non-equilibrium thermodynamics, we demonstrate that a vortex line in a Type-II superconductor carries an entropic quantity $h$ strictly less than $k_B$ per vortex unit (where $k_B$ denotes the Boltzmann constant). This finding establishes a foundation for formulating a revised thermodynamic framework grounded in balance laws, adhering to the principles of local and extended spatial non-equilibrium. Within this model, the vortex line core exhibits lower temperatures and entropies relative to a vacuum; consequently, heat flows from surrounding superconducting regions into the vortex line. This mechanism drives normal electrons toward recombination with a vortex unit, generating a resistive response along the superconducting path. Notably, this derived resistance $h$ aligns closely with experimental data obtained from isotopic variations in $^{3}$He-A and is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the resistance attributed to a single moving magnetic flux line.

This paper addresses the challenge of coordinating spatially dispersed loads to maximize utility, considering individual agents with limited communication capabilities. Introducing a Maximum Entropy Feedback (MEF) strategy, we enable an aggregation unit to transmit a randomly selected load index $i(t)$ based on the current system price $p(t)$ and the specific load characteristic $d_i(t)$ at that price. Under specific technical assumptions regarding demand and cost functions, we demonstrate the existence of a Backlog Equilibrium Price (BEP). Furthermore, we prove that a Dual Backlog Gradient (DBG) algorithm, which operates on the reported index $i(t)$ and MEF, converges to the Dual Equilibrium (DE) utility level. Finally, we present a single-timescale learning adaptation for both the prices within the BEG algorithm and the load characteristics at each node, ensuring the convergence of the DE utility.

This study introduces a novel stock market forecasting approach built on a Conditional Probability Model (CPMP) that integrates social sentiment, alongside technical indicators and historical price/volume data. To address the challenge of sparse and sparse market records, we developed a Hybrid Distillation Framework (HDF) that combines fine-tuning and contrastive learning. HDF first adapts the model using reinforcement fine-tuning based on past performance, subsequently applying contrastive learning to anchor the forecast through sentiment analysis of social media discussions. Testing this method with real-world data reveals that incorporating sentiment-driven insights from HDF-enhanced training significantly improves forecasting accuracy and generalizes well, even on unseen stocks.

The accretion of a companion star by a white dwarf is a primary mechanism for Type Ia supernovae. While single-white dwarf explosions reach the threshold for such events through sufficient mass transfer, the majority of white dwarfs in binary systems exceed the Chandrasekhar limit, prompting researchers to investigate three-body interactions capable of triggering mergers that initiate a supernova. This study conducts a statistical analysis of potential merging scenarios within triple-star systems, evaluating the probability of a supernova-inducing event. The results indicate that approximately 17% of the examined cases result in a successful merger of two white dwarfs; however, only 2% achieve a high-velocity collision sufficient for a supernova trigger under the specific assumptions made. It is important to note that this study evaluates only a minimal subset of the extensive parameter space governing triples containing at least one white dwarf. Consequently, although more complex interactions involving partial or total disruption of the lighter white dwarf exist, our analysis suggests that high-speed binary merges remain a significant pathway for generating Type Ia supernovae.

We examine double Higgs boson production within the Hanff Effective Field Theory (EFT), demonstrating a direct mapping between the leading coefficients of the Higgs effective field theory (Higgs EFT)—derived by integrating out heavy resonances in new physics models—and the standard model effective field theory (SMEFT) coefficients (the orders $1/\Lambda^2$ terms) that significantly influence this process. This correspondence is established on a one-to-one basis, linking leading EFT parameters to specific linear combinations of the roughly 100 relevant $1/\Lambda^2$ coefficients. Consequently, our methodology allows for the determination of the information content encoded in double Higgs production cross sections and differential distributions relative to the vast parameter space of the SMEFT. Consequently, this offers a practical means to evaluate the efficacy of Higgs pair production channels in probing fundamental EFT coefficients governing the Standard Model.

We examined forced granular mixing, focusing on drag forces acting on a cylindrical object traversing two-dimensional granular layers at various speeds. By analyzing experiments across different granular materials, container depths, and movement velocities, we discovered two primary findings. First, drag forces peak at an optimal driving rate; moving too slowly allows time for granular arching to reduce resistance, while rapid motion creates dynamic effects that facilitate fluidization and lowers drag. Second, despite diverse intruder geometries and material parameters, this optimization follows a universal scaling law when driving velocity and force are appropriately normalized. Since efficient mixing correlates with maximal drag, this universal scaling provides a robust framework for planning and controlling forced mixing operations effectively.

Utilising the semi-analytic disk galaxy model known as HiMMOS 2, this study investigates the dynamics and metal enrichment of multi-phase gas outflows within a sample of ten massive, starbursting systems selected from MillenniumDisk to ensure consistent initial conditions. The simulations accurately reproduce key observable features, including radial velocity jumps, X-ray emission, and the morphological structures seen in Hα and absorption spectra. The results indicate that intense bursts of star formation can expel gas on a timescale of approximately 10 million years, potentially explaining the unusually short gas depletion times observed in systems like Mrk 273. Furthermore, while these outflows efficiently drive heavy elements into the circumgalactic medium, they retain enough fuel to sustain elevated star-formation rates for hundreds of Myr, aligning well with predictions derived from X-ray data.

Tuning the hyperparameters of machine learning models is essential for achieving top-tier accuracy. While recent automated methods have aimed to lower the barriers for finding efficient configurations, they often require substantial resources and time to function properly. To address this issue, we present BoAnon, a budget-aware approach that leverages non-stationary bandit algorithms. BoAnon transforms the budget-aware setting into a multi-armed bandit problem by continuously updating its predictions using online methods. Consequently, BoAnon can significantly outperform random strategies, establishing a path toward resolving the budget-aware challenge within non-stationary environments. Our evaluations across multiple real-world scenarios demonstrate BoAnon's robustness and adaptability, showing that it remains effective and able to handle changes in both single-model and ensemble-search budgets. Furthermore, we introduce a complementary online method to determine optimal budget allocations for ensembles, collectively ensuring that BoAnon successfully manages non-stationary environments in various budgeting contexts.

The property of being even-2-factorable (E2F) defines a distinct subset of cubic graphs, permitting the analysis of factors with varying characteristics. This study proposes an implementation of Li's variant of the Bateman-Horn Conjecture to approximate prime-generating counts for subsets of quadratic expressions that partially but not wholly do so. System call (syscall) filtering is a widely adopted technique for mitigating syscalls-attacks, which have historically plagued predominantly compiled languages. This research investigates the feasibility of applying such mitigation to interpreted environments, specifically targeting PHP and Python web services. To address the challenges posed by interpretation overhead and dynamic code execution, we introduce Timeloops, an efficient, syscall-level filter that utilizes a fixed, timed loop structure. This design ensures competitive performance while managing the trade-offs between safety constraints and dynamic behavior. Our comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that Timeloops successfully filters over 90% of syscalls for both tested configurations, achieving excellent performance: it reaches 51.8 syscalls per second for a single PHP instance and 1,023 syscalls per second for two concurrent Python instances.

This work analyzes the implications of dark matter (DM) exhibiting both a pseudo-Goldstone boson nature and belonging to a non-trivial global matter symmetry for its elastic interactions with nucleons. Furthermore, the requirement of the symmetry mandates that the field shifts under the symmetry transformation, which suppresses scattering at long wavelengths by the inverse of the symmetry breaking scale. Collectively, these mechanisms suppress "low-$E_{\rm reco}$" events in direct detection experiments, thereby enhancing the parameter space allowable for direct searches while remaining largely untested in other sectors. Although this scenario is heavily constrained by cosmology and collider data, current limits from precision measurements and exotic hadron studies still permit dark matter comprising the pseudo-Goldstone boson within the simplest global symmetry models.

This study introduces the concept of an all-optical diode/quasi-circulator utilizing unidirectional coupling between microresonators mediated by chirality. We demonstrate that the switching operation of these components is achieved through chiriral interresonator coupling, specifically leveraging chirality-based anti-crossing phenomena to control light circulation. Underlying this functionality is a mechanism where switching and operating currents modulate the coupling by shifting the system across an anti-crossing point. Our findings indicate that this approach supports a broad light circulation state, characterized by high contrast ratios between switching currents and distinct advantages regarding sensitivity to switching current variations, offering enhanced adaptability and precision.

We report on a coordinated, multi-wavelength observation campaign conducted during the 2019 outburst of the Galactic microquasar IGR J19294+1816, which included instruments from RXTE, NuSTAR, XMM-Newton, and ground-based optical/IR facilities. Analysis of X-ray data reveals a complex spectral state characterized by the simultaneous presence of a hard power-law component and a thermally modeled disk emission. Furthermore, distinct spectral features were detected across various phases of the outburst cycle, coinciding with optical observations that tracked significant variability in the optical flux. Correlating these findings suggests a connection between fluctuations in the accretion disk and the high-energy X-ray and $\gamma$-ray emissions. Consequently, future monitoring in both optical and high-energy bands is essential for deciphering the emission mechanisms associated with this source and similar objects.

The evolving landscape of 5G networks necessitates advanced scheduling protocols capable of managing information and energy delivery simultaneously. To support this, the TFIET scheme prioritizes data scheduling based on a user's specific scheduling request (SR) and subsequently schedules energy using an inverse relationship to UE channel conditions, ensuring efficient resource allocation for both dimensions. To evaluate the system's performance, a novel "ded2D-2D-condition-function" (DCF) is developed. This function integrates key variables such as the TFIET scheduling policy, the distribution of data files, and the statistical characteristics of energy harvestable energy at UE levels. Simulation outcomes demonstrate the system's robustness in handling data and energy scheduling under diverse data file configurations and UE energy harvesting profiles.

The increasing popularity of video-on-demand streaming relies heavily on cloud services to maintain Quality of Service. Dopamine is critical to the physics of doped graphene, yet experimental techniques for determining its concentration remain constrained. We demonstrate that specific heat serves as a reliable alternative by showing that it is linearly proportional to doping level within the random potential approximation. This linearity persists across a wide range of temperatures and remains valid even when considering the full, complex microscopic details of disorder. The findings align closely with experimental data from Johnsson et al. [Nature Phys. 11, 74 (2015)] regarding Joule heating measurements, specifically the specific heat derived from their stress test protocol. Because this method relies on well-established principles and yields distinct signatures, it presents a promising avenue for specific heat-based detection of doping levels in graphene samples.

Coping with the ongoing cosmic chronology puzzle involves exploring extended dark energy (EDE) scenarios where dark energy constitutes a minor component of the dark sector ($f_{\rm EDE} < 1$). We first establish permissible ranges for $f_{\rm EDE}$ based on these small-scale field limits and the radiation-domination transition, finding these ranges shift notably with variations in the cosmological model parameters. Our results indicate that, within an extended sector framework where EDE comprises a minor fraction, specific scenarios can resolve both sides of the cosmic-age puzzle, yielding an allowed $f_{\rm EDE}$ range of approximately $6.2 \sim 10^{-1}$ eV field values. Consequently, the flexibility inherent in allowing EDE fraction to vary within this extended framework enables us to achieve solutions that fixed-parameter models struggle to reach.

Synthesizing high-quality single crystals on graphene substrates offers a pathway to decouple electronic properties from the substrate's lattice, allowing access to novel states restricted by lattice matching constraints. On graphene, this constraint is further relaxed by graphene's fractional sublattice preference, which facilitates the formation of distinct epitaxial domains oriented along specific directions dictated by this preference. Consequently, the spatial arrangement of these domains becomes a critical factor influencing the resulting material properties. In this study, we investigate the formation of such domains during the epitaxial growth of CuMn$_2$O$_4$ single crystals on graphene-covered Si(111) substrates, varying the process across different growth temperatures. Single-crystal characterization via X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and atomic force microscopy reveals a temperature-dependent domain distribution: elevated temperatures suppress domain formation, yielding solely the (100) domain, whereas lower temperatures yield a mixture of domains with the (110) domain exhibiting superior crystalline quality. Furthermore, electrical transport measurements on thin films indicate that the (100) domain possesses a larger antiferromagnetic order parameter than the (110) domain. Collectively, these findings provide a strategic route for tailoring the properties of single crystals grown on graphene through engineering of domain formation.

This study addresses a problem of polymer mixing in a heterogeneous porous medium. The goal involves determining a minimal-cost injection strategy to achieve a desired concentration distribution within the domain. To this effect, we formulate an optimal control framework governed by an advection-reaction system. The viscosity dynamics within the model follow a non-newtonian power law dependent on local polymer viscosity. What distinguishes our approach is the incorporation of free boundaries arising from non-smooth feedback laws applied to the viscosity model. By leveraging a one-to-one connection between these free boundary problems and parabolic variational inequalities, we establish the existence of an optimal solution. Furthermore, to compute this solution practically, we devise a gradient-based numerical scheme. Convergence tests for this algorithm demonstrate how varying viscosity parameters alter both the injected polymer profiles and the resulting mixing outcomes.

We evaluated this method on two datasets, comparing it against three established labeling techniques. Results show that annotators found our approach more accurate, requiring less time, and producing higher-quality multi-label images compared to baseline approaches. We also analyzed label distribution, demonstrating that an imbalanced datasets can be effectively corrected by our method through an automated, balanced labeling process. Furthermore, we assessed the utility of these generated multi-label images for supervised learning, showing that models using our annotated images achieve state-of-the-art performance.

The MAGIC collaboration recently reported on the lack of GeV gamma rays in the Coma cluster using the "MAD" model, attributing this absence to GeV emission suppression caused by the quenching of cosmic ray (CR) hadron interactions in high-electron environments. This paper demonstrates analytically that the rate at which electrons heat up is a deciding factor in determining how effectively the MAD model explains observed TeV gamma rays in galaxy clusters specifically. Through a simplified yet effective modeling approach, we analyze how different thermalization mechanisms and initial high-electron conditions shape the final CR and photon spectra. Our findings indicate that the proposed MAD framework can successfully explain the GeV/TeV data of the Coma cluster if the electron heating rate remains below approximately $1 \times 10^{80} \text{ erg s}^{-2}$, which is notably lower than the $10^{82} \text{ erg s}^{-2}$ value observed in the source. However, this upper limit for the heating rate is significantly higher—reaching up to $10^{81} \text{ erg s}^{-2}$—in the case of the Abell 2219 cluster, where the MAGIC observatory has detected GeV gamma rays that align well with the model. Therefore, this phenomenon offers a distinct method for testing various physical mechanisms governing the high-electron plasma states in massive galaxy clusters.

This study introduces a novel approach to modeling asset return distributions by analyzing the mathematical connection between cross-sectional slices of return distributions and individual assets' component parts. By leveraging this insight, we derive an expression for the first four moments (mean, skewness, kurtosis) of these fragments. Applying this knowledge, we propose a new dynamic factor model in which the mean and higher-order moments of return distributional fragments are regressed against various profile characteristics. Empirical analysis shows that this model outperforms the traditional HFR Index in explaining the clustering of cryptocurrency assets, with additional robustness tests confirming these outcomes.

This study introduces a novel, data-driven method utilizing Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (c-Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks) to enhance the detection and classification of cardiac abnormalities by conditioning inputs on specific target classes. Instead of manually constructing an augmented dataset through repetitive, user-guided relabeling of videos to a target category—a process that introduces unnecessary noise and redundancy—the proposed method uses unmodified, heterogeneous data drawn from diverse sources. Furthermore, due to the unsupervised nature of training on this varied collection, the system is expected to function effectively in clinical settings when generating specific pathologies for analysis using only uncurated, real-world input.

Existing federated learning approaches for activity recognition on wearable devices are hindered by the need for pre-extracted features, a step that requires specialized hardware and increases privacy risks due to data leaving the device. This work examines the potential of asymmetric leptoquark (LQ) pairs to distinguish between the LQ charge assignments in the $e\text{-}\mu$ LQ scenario, where single LQs are produced via lepton-flavordisplaced lepton fusion at linear colliders. We analyze the applicable production mechanisms and final states, with an emphasis on the asymmetric top quark-antiquark current LQs. Effective operation of this asymmetry requires the parton distribution functions to yield a higher average partonic center-of-mass energy for initial-state muons than for electrons. Consequently, this requirement dictates that the asymmetry parameter must be relatively large, and the production yield is further constrained by the LQ mass relative to the collision center-of-mass energy. We determine parameter regions detectable at both CLIC and ILC based on LQ mass and branching ratios into specific final states, noting that the resulting signatures differ notably depending on whether the LQ is vector or scalar. Although Relevance Learning is a novel strategy for identifying predictive features that capitalizes on existing labeled and extensively characterized datasets to "learn" the utility of newly added features, its application to time-series expression data remains untested. This study focuses on a set of initial expression measurements for a panel of features and a smaller set of time-point expressions incorporating those same features. Leveraging primary data from the Coriell Institute, we applied our revised Relevance Learning algorithm to expression profiles of 6,198 features across 72 individuals at a single time point, utilizing individual identities and demographic information learned from all 6,198 features for prediction. Subsequently, we assessed the remaining expression data for these "SmartSeq" features to identify which required labeling based on the initial learned relevance scores. The study evaluated two distinct labeling protocols: one where labeling costs were uniform per feature, and another where costs varied based on the initial relevance scores. Results demonstrated that applying this methodology to identify race, age, sex, and ancestry-specific features yielded substantial efficiencies, reducing labeling requirements by 94.8% for race, 98.0% for age, 98.8% for sex, and 97.4% for population structure when accounting for variable costs. These findings indicate that Relevance Learning offers a significant advantage in streamlining high-throughput labeling for large-scale genomic investigations involving multiple time points.

Although prototypical networks offer speed and efficiency in few-shot learning, they frequently fail when few examples are available if all class prototypes must be updated simultaneously. To address this limitation in musical instrument identification from audio recordings under a few-shot setting, we introduce a novel Hierarchical Few-Shot Prototypical Network (HFSP). This framework employs two sets of adaptably learned class prototypes organized within a broader task prototype. By utilizing a dual-level loss function that minimizes distances between a query prototype and its corresponding subset of task prototype, as well as between the query prototype and individual class prototypes, HFSP achieves an even more robust task representation. Experiments confirm that this method not only matches existing state-of-the results in few-shot classification accuracy but also demonstrates superior generalization across different sets of classification tasks.

We introduce a methodology for creating Pruned DNA Data Storage (PDDS) systems, which replace conventional concatemers with short primers. A storage partition in this system is defined by the set of primers flanking it; during retrieval, these primers facilitate the selective amplification of corresponding partitions through in vitro synthesis. This work highlights how combinatorial DNA synthesis paired with standard short-read sequencing enables efficient encoding, decoding, and management of information in DNA. To mitigate errors stemming from sequencing and DNA degradation, this approach leverages a random error-correcting scheme known as sparse repeated sequencing (SRS). In this study, we examine a high-resolution, full-resolution cosmological simulation covering a 12$^{\circ}$ volume, specifically tracking 888 individual dark-matter halos as they evolve from redshift 4 down to 1. Using a new, automated method, we identified 15,584 distinct halos experiencing accretion streams within a timeframe. We present a detailed statistical characterization of these streams, noting how their frequency, mass, and physical attributes shift with redshift and the target halo's properties. Furthermore, by comparing these observed statistics against various theoretical predictions, we found remarkable agreement regarding how stream properties depend on halo mass and evolutionary stage (redshift). Finally, we highlight several distinct populations of halos defined by stream characteristics, suggesting that future observational efforts could map these groups to better trace the cosmic assembly history revealed through accretion dynamics.

We analyze the low-energy and high-energy physical manifestations of the Universal Texture Zero (UTZ) model, an approach where neutrino texture zeros are grounded in left-right symmetry. Within this model, a texture zero arises when a left-handed neutrino partner mixes with left-handed partners in a way that suppresses its mass to near-zero levels. We determine the properties of the heavy, inaccessible neutrinos associated with the UTZ seesaw mechanism by analyzing the lighter, observable sector. Focusing on texture zeros present in both neutrino and quark mass matrices, we evaluate the specific predictions for particle masses and cosmological scales. Our results indicate that the model predicts a normal mass ordering for neutrinos, with the lightest mass state ($m_1$) remaining nearly massless. Additionally, the unique constraints of the UTZ framework generate specific correlations linking scales observable in neutrino oscillations, beta decay, early universe processes, and other high-energy phenomena.

Reversible encryption enables authorized parties, like government authorities, to compel decryption of data using a specific "backdoor" or private key, a feature that has become increasingly common in modern cryptography. To address this, we introduce the concept of Deniable Reversible Encryption (DRE)—a reversible encryption scheme that ensures data authenticators cannot be compelled to deny their authorship, even if the data is later decrypted. Empirical results demonstrate that by mitigating the limitations of traditional data annotation methods, MetaFEND effectively detects fake news even when the training dataset contains newly labeled items.

Utilizing these updated parameters, we developed a comprehensive model calculating exchange couplings for arbitrary donor arrangements, revealing that exchange interactions extending to the third neighbor are significant enough to warrant inclusion in future quantum simulations and engineering endeavors.

Although Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in object recognition and image classification tasks, their efficacy heavily relies on accurately labeled data. By specifically and precisely targeting erroneous regions rather than applying blind modifications, DASDAMD enhances the diversity of training data while preserving crucial semantic features. Experimental outcomes confirm that DASDAMD not only improves classification metrics across various scenarios but also achieves rapid and precise convergence during the training phase.

This paper investigates a scenario where light interacts with two distinct two-level systems within a confined cavity governed by strong coupling and the single-photon regime. We demonstrate that when light is initially in a coherent state entering with an almost deterministic number of photons, and the cavity interacts sequentially with two otherwise uncorrelated incoming atoms, the resulting atomic state can be highly entangled despite the cavity maintaining significant residual photons after each interaction. Consequently, under these specific conditions, a cavity linked by a optical field to an atom acts as an effective component for generating substantial multipartite entanglement, even when the incident cavity-atom system is not itself entangled. However, if the intracavity light is instead a single photon, this multipartite generation is suppressed; in this case, the optical field functions merely as a resource for generating pairwise entanglement between consecutive atoms, acting similarly to a link shared between two individual pair entanglement states. This study proposes a new, two-step strategy to classify tweet sentiment using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. Empirical results indicate that this dual-phase approach significantly enhances the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores of the sentiment classification process compared to using retweets-containing data directly.

Non-linear electrodynamics and non-linear Yang-Mills theories yield a far richer and more diverse spectrum of black hole solutions compared to standard general relativity coupled only to linear electromagnetic or Yang-Mills fields. Immersive streaming represents a crucial evolution in the delivery of remote experiences, such as virtual tours and telepresence applications, by allowing users to select their viewing areas within a three-dimensional environment known as the "viewport." These findings indicate that subtitle-supported streamlines the user's viewdirection adjustment process following a camera shift, thereby improving overall viewobject prediction performance and delivering a more seamless user experience.

Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is highly effective for reducing annotation costs, a necessity in fields like medical image segmentation where precise labeling is difficult and costly. Interpolation-based methods are commonly used in semi-supervised classification to regularize student models by constraining predictions at interpolation endpoints. To address this limitation, we introduce a new approach that respects the geometric structure of segmentation masks. Our method first interpolates the input images corresponding to the distribution being predicted and subsequently constrains the overlap between the resulting segmentation and these interpolated images. Additionally, we incorporate a distribution-matching term aligned with the interpolated images to further refine the regularization. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on two publicly available datasets: the Pancreatic Segmentation Contest 2 and the Medical Segmentation Qualification 2, both of which focus on reticular organs such as the pancreas. We have also evaluated our method on the Human Cell Atlas project, analyzing cell mask segmentation across diverse biological cell types characterized by intricate internal structures.

Consequently, our derived limits on the dark-matter fraction involving PBHs are substantially tighter than those resulting from subhalofraction estimates based on simply counting satellite dark matter subhalos.

Theoretical calculations confirm that raft dynamics are dominated by particle re-assembly speeds relative to fluid divergence during early stages, whereas competition between reconstruction and separation mechanisms controls evolution in later stages. The provided model effectively mirrors actual geologic phenomena observed within Earth's tectonic boundaries.

The proposed framework categorizes into four distinct designs based on whether beamforming is coherent or incoherent and whether the SI level is fixed or variable. The paper derives geometric conditions indicating when optimal power allocation shifts between free (unconstrained) and boundary (constrained) states for each design variant, formulating the corresponding optimization challenges accordingly. Specifically, variants with variable SI power are addressed using a branch-and-bound algorithm, whereas those with fixed SI power are solved via convex reformulation techniques. Numerical evaluations confirm the effectiveness of these algorithms and demonstrate that boundary power allocation yields superior security outcomes compared to free allocation in certain configurations.

We demonstrate the generation of non-local entangled states utilizing individual non-linear quantum emitters integrated into the system alongside topologically-protected electromagnetic (MEs). Through the interference of light from non-linear emitters, we take advantage of spatial positioning of the emitters relative to the two directions traveling in opposite edge modes. By employing third-order saturation emitters, we utilize intensity-dependent frequency shifts within these edge modes to achieve cross-gain modulation and between the two signal paths in opposite directions. As a result, we can create a non-local entangled photon using single non-linear emitters. Further, we investigate potential impacts arising from deconfinement issues, device imperfections, and also explore the application of our approach in quantum repeaters networks.

By incorporating safety constraints and leveraging the dynamic characteristics of human-driven vehicles ahead, our proposed framework ensures robustness across varying traffic conditions while maintaining compliance with current highway codes. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach effectively enhances safety and throughput in complex intersection environments compared to traditional single-phase trajectory methods.

This work examines the application of the Mott-Seitz framework for estimating the minimum energy barrier (EB) for nonradiative decay in relation to phosphorescent zinc complexes. The initial analysis utilizes a simplified three-state model, which positions radiative and nonradiative states within a Landau-Lifshits-Zener (LZ) two-state model framework. Radiative state inclusion is handled via an optimal unitary transformation applied to the LZ model. Calculations indicate that predicting the $EB$ using the full three-state model introduces negligible deviation compared to the approximation derived from the LZ model. Subsequently, applying the Mott-Seitz approach yields an approximate EB value that diverges significantly from both model predictions and standard experimental data regarding Zn-based zincocarboxyl zinc complexes. To rectify this discrepancy, an enhanced version of the Mott-Seitz model is subsequently developed; this refined formulation brings calculated $EB$ results into close alignment with observed experimental values. The distinct model discrepancies are primarily attributed to the simplifications of potential energy landscape surface assumptions and the neglect of intermediate states inherent to the original Zn-based Mott-Seitz approach.

Introducing a novel algorithm to train sparsity-constrained neural networks, this approach sparsifies deep architectures without requiring post-training sparsification. Differences in weight updates are calculated via an adapted variant of the Spared Propagation technique, revised specifically to handle angular parameter-based connectivity constraints. This alteration results in a significant decrease in parameters relative to conventional backpropagation. Furthermore, by incorporating adaptation of the topology-controlling variable through an end-to-to end gradient process, the algorithm avoids heuristic methods. This unique design enables seamless integration of learned, significant connectivity patterns within the network without introducing overhead. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach achieves superior accuracy on several tasks, including image classification and natural language inference, while offering more efficient gradient usage compared to previous methods.

Diffusion models are increasingly utilized for generating medical imagery; however, adversarial code injections into their latent spaces can generate misleading or non-diagnostic content, potentially compromising patient safety. This study examines generative attacks and defenses within the context of diffusion models, establishing a baseline of defensive strategies by adapting methods effective in discriminative generative models. The proposed baseline detects adversarial noise and applies corrections to counter attacks against diffusion models. Furthermore, we introduce our primary contribution, Diffusion Latent Manipulation (DLM), a targeted generative attack designed to inject maximal semantic deception into latent space. The DL approach evaluates success rates and calculates the distance from reference conditions using a Time-of-check versus Time-of-use comparison framework. The proposed DL serves as a testbed for exploring additional defensive mechanisms, with results indicating that the proposed defensive baseline outstrips that of previously adapted methods when combating DL. The proposed framework is computationally efficient, requiring no retraining or model fine-tuning post-inference, and effectively mitigates DL threats, representing a substantial advancement in the state of the art.

Multidimensional (MD) data visualization tools are essential for analysts, as they enable the efficient exploration of data through views that maintain visual coherence. A key challenge remains allowing users to add and remove visual encodings dynamically while preserving their ability to compare, interpret, and infer from the views. Existing methods for selecting these encodings typically depend on hard-coded analytical patterns, which hampers the rapid integration of new channels. To overcome this limitation, we introduce "Learned Analytical Patterns," or LAPs—a general framework that enables the composition of views by learning patterns from a single base image generated when new channels become available. We further present "ViDaExpert," an end-to-end system that accepts both isolated images and dynamic multidimensional visualization environments. By accepting keyboard commands to add or remove encoding channels, "ViDaExpert" utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify and generate other views associated with those specific patterns during analysis sessions. Utilizing functional similarity measures, we evaluate this system against others, demonstrating its superior support for flexible data exploration.

The scheme utilizes a High-Mid Low (HLM) hierarchy, where pre-computed Jacobian matrices allow for coordinate transformation between physical and parametric spaces to remain consistent across all grid levels, requiring computation solely on the element of the finest mesh. The results demonstrate that this algorithm achieves high accuracy and efficiency, significantly outperforming conventional approaches in both speed efficiency and overall performance.
